stories.title: The Candle Can Hear The Electricity
stories.description: On a very quiet November morning, a glass of cold-brewed green tea is placed above a small candle flame, slowly warming to a gentle drinking temperature. The room is so still that the candle seems able to hear the faint electricity moving through the walls, while the green tea listens to the autumn leaves outside. Across the streets, fallen leaves continue to cover the city like a golden-brown flood, gathering along pavements and around the feet of trees. Nothing urgent happens: the flame flickers, the tea gradually warms, and the last traces of autumn remain outside the window. Between the almost inaudible sounds of the room and the immense silence of the city, a November morning quietly begins.

stories.title: Seven Dances For The Changing Moon
stories.description: In the middle of autumn, beneath the great full moon of the Moon Festival, a large family of wild rabbits gathers to dance among the brilliantly colored leaves. They love the moon so deeply that they decide to dance for it every day, even as its shape and place in the sky change. Sometimes the moon shines above them at night, sometimes it appears pale against the blue afternoon, and sometimes it is only a slender crescent above the trees. As the weeks pass, the rabbits continue dancing through golden afternoons, windy evenings, bare November forests, and the first cold mornings of winter. Their dances change with the light, the weather, and the gradual disappearance of autumn, but their devotion to the moon remains unchanged. Finally, beneath a new full moon shining over the first snow, the rabbits dance again, their small feet moving across the white earth where the autumn leaves once lay.
